If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this policy change depends on interpreting the current multi-wake evidence. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf or neighboring configurations.

The contract confirms the required order: observations and keyframes must be interpreted before any policy edit, then the visual diagnosis must be written before changing the candidate. I’m now inventorying the assigned parent, sampled results, inherited optimizer notes, and the existing policy while keeping the candidate untouched.

The sampled set has no success: the strongest scalar result is `dbfcc8041ceb` (progress `0.517`, closest `3.03L`), while `bf5ebfa0ffca` is the most informative near-approach failure (closest `2.67L` but worse mean/final distance and an upper exit). Per the visual-signal skill, I’m inspecting the shared prewarm and both released trajectories before deciding whether the existing receding-distance repair is justified.

The images and diagnostics agree on the failure mechanism: every variant self-propels upstream, enters the developed multi-wake corridor, then rotates into a large upper hook; the closest-approach recovery variant reaches `2.67L` but reverses the bearing command whenever distance temporarily recedes, loses upstream travel, and still exits high. I’m checking the inherited optimizer notes now to separate mechanisms already falsified from the untested lateral-translation signal suggested by the parent guidance.

The reusable gap is now concrete: the sampled receding-speed proxy activates on any temporary distance increase, while the policy’s `bearing` deliberately discards the sign of forward target projection. I’ll record the diagnosis before editing, then build one candidate that preserves the best `0.35` phase-headroom anchor while using normalized body-frame forward target sign to reverse only the mean posterior bearing request after the fish passes the target’s longitudinal plane.

The policy now preserves the strongest sampled upstream mechanism and changes only how the target-bearing request behaves at longitudinal overshoot. Before validation, I’m revising the durable experience bank to close the stale lateral-velocity recommendation and distinguish the positive phase-headroom result from the failed receding/load repairs.

Both required provenance files are updated, and the candidate remains a single non-empty policy file. I’m moving to contract validation now: parameter ownership, Julia parsing, prohibited-signal checks, and the mandated check-runner review; no CFD will be run.

The mandated mock contract does not expose the convenience field `forward_distance_L`, so I expressed the same normalized signed projection through the public `target_body_L` vector (`-target_body_L[1]`). I’m now invoking the configured check-runner exactly as required; it will perform only lightweight contract and boundary checks, not CFD.
